title: Ray Nance in Earl Hines's band
summary: Nance was his closest friend in the band, a violinist and Louis-style trumpeter and showman, whom Ellington praised.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: So, I don't know, that was a fast resume of the guys in the band with Earl. And, of course, as I mentioned previously that the guy I was more close to in that band was Ray Nance. And the reason I remember him so well was Ray was a fine musician and he had his own little group before he came with Earl. He had a fine little group and they were all youngsters playing around Chicago. And Ray always was a fine violinist. I think he played violin before he did trumpet.

But he admired Louis tremendously and, in fact, all of us did in those days. And so, he played trumpet on the style of Louis, and he sang a lot of Louis' things that Louis did. And he did a heck of a job because he could dance also, you know.

He was a terrific showman. And as most people found out when he went with Duke, he really got the proper exposure with Duke. And Duke admired him. Duke told us that Ray Nance never played a wrong note. You know, I thought that was a beautiful statement that he made about him.
